headline: Growth accelerates, guidance raised despite GAAP profit dip
summary_short: IQVIA reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.37B, up 8.7% y/y on record R&D Solutions bookings, while GAAP diluted EPS was roughly flat at $1.53 (basic $1.54) as restructuring and interest costs weighed; the company raised full-year guidance.
summary_long: Revenue grew 8.7% y/y (8.5% constant-currency) to $4.37B, led by R&D Solutions' 8.8% growth on record $3.15B net new bookings (19% y/y, 1.22x book-to-bill) and 8.6% Commercial Solutions growth from patient-solutions, engagement and AI-adoption strength. Gross profit rose 8.5% y/y to $1.44B. Higher restructuring costs ($63M vs $32M), SG&A, D&A and interest expense pushed GAAP net income down 3.8% y/y to $256M and diluted EPS roughly flat at $1.53, even as Adjusted Diluted EPS rose 12.1% y/y to $3.15 on non-GAAP addbacks. Cash was $1.91B against $16.0B debt (3.59x net leverage); the company repurchased $398M of stock this quarter. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue ($17,275-17,475M), Adjusted EBITDA ($4,000-4,050M) and Adjusted Diluted EPS ($12.80-13.00).

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by 8.8% R&D Solutions growth on record $3.15B net new bookings (1.22x book-to-bill) and 8.6% Commercial Solutions growth from patient solutions, commercial engagement and AI-solutions adoption.
Cost of revenues grew ~8.9% y/y, roughly in line with revenue's 8.7%, so gross margin was nearly flat; the release does not separately narrate gross-margin drivers.
Not narrated in prose, but the income statement shows restructuring costs nearly doubled y/y ($63M vs $32M) and SG&A rose 12.8%, outpacing revenue growth at the operating-cost line.
Below the operating line, interest expense rose 8.2% y/y and a $3M loss on debt extinguishment was recorded, further compounding the operating-cost pressure noted above.

GAAP diluted EPS held roughly flat despite lower net income because diluted shares fell 3.4% y/y on continued buybacks ($398M this quarter); Adjusted Diluted EPS rose 12.1% as non-GAAP addbacks more than offset the GAAP decline.
CEO cited a strengthening market and results exceeding the high end of expectations for revenue, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EPS, pointing to sustained momentum into 2027.
